5.text: Such frames usually consist of four stout uprights firmly embedded in

6.text: the ground, with cross-bars tied to their upper ends, and a platform made of

7.text: poles, or of bone of whale, laid across the bars. Some of these simple

8.text: structures were erected on the cliffs overhanging the sea. During the winter-

9.text: time, if any of the seal-hunters were overtaken by a storm on the open ice,

10.text: these platforms served as beacons: the women ascended them, carrying burning

11.text: lamps under their transparent overcoats of walrus-gut, and stood there for

12.text: hours, shouting, and displaying their lights to guide the wanderers. Over the

13.text: platform a light bunch of feathers, called pag̣g̣oˊlhɪn (“vane”), was suspended

14.text: from a thin staff. It was consulted by the hunter in observations of wind

15.text: and weather. Such vanes are still in use among the Maritime Chukchee, and

16.text: even among those who are settled on the Middle Anadyr.
